ids: test/gate_item2/mediated-real-provider.test.ts::recovery around an impounded identity is refused, not resumed (target-only)
target_only_tests.why: One case, not counted as ported coverage, added by continuo#92 (D-0047). `start` and `resume` share `#spawn` and therefore shared the defect, but interlock's suite drives the identity mismatch only through `start`. This case takes the resume half over the real provider with the race removed rather than reduced: the incident is already persisted when the walk begins, so there is no child left to lose a race to and `resume` answers with the record's own incident deterministically. It also pins the property the class change exists to protect -- no second writer is minted on an impounded id (the spawn log stays at one entry) and the binding still says `spawned`/`unobserved`.

approved_non_running.reason: The source's two capability gates -- @pytest.mark.skipif(not HAS_PROC, ...) on the adoption case and @pytest.mark.skipif(not IS_POSIX, ...) on the resume case -- are the same two conditions test/session/claude-cli-provider.test.ts's ledger (parity/session.claude-cli-provider.ledger.json) already approves for that file, reused here verbatim rather than re-derived: `IS_POSIX = process.platform !== "win32"` and `HAS_PROC = statSync("/proc", { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isDirectory() === true`, both probed at module load exactly as pytest evaluates a skipif condition at collection time, never inferred from the platform name (rule 4 of docs/test-translation-conventions.md -- HAS_PROC is the narrower condition, since macOS is POSIX without /proc). The two reasons are carried at their call sites verbatim from the source's decorator arguments.
